questions.text: As per the table below showing India's rank in the Global Innovation Index (GII) published by WIPO for select years, which period recorded the highest average annual improvement in rank (i.e., largest average drop in rank number per year)? | Year | Rank | | :--- | :--- | | 2015 | 81 | | 2019 | 52 | | 2021 | 46 | | 2023 | 40 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate 'Improvement per Year' = (Rank Start - Rank End) / (Years Gap). Compare the ratios without full division. Option A: Improvement 29 over 4 years (~7.25/yr). Option B: Improvement 6 over 2 years (3/yr). Option C: Improvement 6 over 2 years (3/yr). Option D: Improvement 41 over 8 years (~5.1/yr). Option A has the highest rate. Worked Solution: 2015-2019: Rank improved from 81 to 52 (Δ=29) in 4 years → 7.25 ranks/year. 2019-2021: 52 to 46 (Δ=6) in 2 years → 3 ranks/year. 2021-2023: 46 to 40 (Δ=6) in 2 years → 3 ranks/year. Overall 2015-2023: 81 to 40 (Δ=41) in 8 years → 5.125 ranks/year. The highest average annual improvement occurred in 2015-2019.

questions.text: Arrange the following events of the Indian Freedom Struggle in correct chronological order: 1. August Offer 2. Cripps Mission 3. Quit India Movement 4. Cabinet Mission Select the correct code.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Anchor known years. August Offer (1940) is earliest; Cabinet Mission (1946) is latest. This eliminates C and D. Between 1942 events: Cripps Mission (March 1942) preceded Quit India Movement (August 1942). Worked Solution: 1. August Offer (Aug 1940); 2. Cripps Mission (Mar 1942); 3. Quit India Movement (Aug 1942); 4. Cabinet Mission (Mar 1946). Sequence 1-2-3-4 is correct.

questions.text: With reference to the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act, 2023, which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It subsumes the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) established in 2008.

options.label: B
options.text: The Governing Board is chaired by the Union Minister of Science and Technology.

options.label: C
options.text: The Executive Council is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Science and Technology.

options.label: D
options.text: It provides for a financial corpus entirely funded by private sector contributions.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options with incorrect chairpersons. The ANRF Act mandates the Prime Minister as ex-officio President of the Governing Board (not Science Minister) and the Principal Scientific Adviser as Chairperson of the Executive Council (not Secretary, DST). The funding is primarily governmental (Rs 50,000 crore over 5 years, 28% govt share), not entirely private. Option A is the only factually accurate statement: the Act repeals the SERB Act, 2008, subsuming SERB into ANRF. Full Solution: The ANRF Act, 2023 establishes the Anusandhan National Research Foundation to seed, grow and promote R&D. Section 24 repeals the Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008, dissolving SERB and transferring its assets/liabilities to ANRF. The Governing Board is headed by the PM (President) and Union Ministers of S&T and Education (Vice-Presidents). The Executive Council is chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser. The total estimated cost is Rs 50,000 crore (2023-28), with Rs 14,000 crore (28%) from Govt of India and the rest from non-government sources.

questions.text: As per the table below showing sectoral deployment of bank credit (outstanding) and year-on-year growth rates for a recent period, which sector contributed the maximum absolute increment (in ₹ Lakh Crore) to the total credit outstanding over the year? | Sector | Outstanding (₹ Lakh Cr) | Y-o-Y Growth (%) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Agriculture & Allied | 15.5 | 15.0 | | Industry | 32.0 | 8.0 | | Services | 38.5 | 20.0 | | Personal Loans | 34.0 | 18.0 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare absolute increments using Base × Growth% approximation without exact multiplication. Agriculture: 15.5 × 0.15 ≈ 2.3; Industry: 32 × 0.08 ≈ 2.6; Services: 38.5 × 0.20 ≈ 7.7; Personal Loans: 34 × 0.18 ≈ 6.1. Services has the highest product. Worked Solution: Absolute Increment = Outstanding × (Growth%/100). Agriculture = 2.325; Industry = 2.56; Services = 7.7; Personal Loans = 6.12. Services contributes the maximum absolute increment.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the approximate installed capacity of major renewable energy sources in India (as of March 2024), what is the approximate combined percentage share of Wind and Bio Power in the total installed renewable capacity (including Large Hydro)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Round Total Capacity (82+46+47+11 = 186 GW) to 180 GW. Round Combined Wind & Bio (46+11 = 57 GW) to 60 GW. Approximate Share = 60/180 = 1/3 ≈ 33.3%. Since actual numerator (57) and denominator (186) are both slightly lower than estimates, the real value is marginally below 33.3%, closest to 31%. Worked Solution: Total Capacity = 82 + 46 + 47 + 11 = 186 GW. Wind + Bio Capacity = 46 + 11 = 57 GW. Percentage = (57 / 186) × 100 = 30.64% ≈ 31%.

questions.text: Arrange the following major mountain passes of India from North to South: 1. Zojila Pass 2. Shipki La Pass 3. Nathu La Pass 4. Palghat Gap Select the correct sequence using the code given below.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Anchor the extremes. Zojila (Ladakh) is the northernmost; Palghat Gap (Western Ghats, Kerala/TN) is the southernmost. Eliminate options not starting with 1 or ending with 4. Only Option A (1-2-3-4) and B (1-3-2-4) remain. Shipki La (Himachal Pradesh) lies north of Nathu La (Sikkim). Correct order: Zojila → Shipki La → Nathu La → Palghat Gap. Worked Solution: Latitudes: Zojila (~34°N), Shipki La (~31°N), Nathu La (~27°N), Palghat (~10°N). Sequence 1-2-3-4 is correct.

questions.text: As per the chart below showing the approximate weightage of major groups in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) Combined (Base 2012=100) for India, if the weight of 'Food and Beverages' is 45.86% and 'Fuel and Light' is 6.84%, what is the approximate combined weight of the remaining groups (Core Inflation components: Housing, Clothing, Miscellaneous)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total weight = 100%. Core Weight = 100% - (Food % + Fuel %). Calculation: 100 - (45.86 + 6.84) = 100 - 52.70 = 47.30%. Use complement rule. Step-by-step: 1. Identify given weights: Food & Beverages = 45.86%, Fuel & Light = 6.84%. 2. Sum given weights: 45.86 + 6.84 = 52.70%. 3. Subtract from total (100%): 100.00 - 52.70 = 47.30%. 4. Option A matches. Option B is the sum of excluded items (trap). Option C/D are random.

questions.text: The Chairperson and Members of which of the following bodies are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a Selection Committee comprising the Prime Minister, Speaker of Lok Sabha, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Chief Justice of India (or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by CJI), and an eminent jurist?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Elimination by Committee Composition. CVC: PM, Home Minister, LoP. CBI Director: PM, CJI, LoP. NHRC: PM, Home Minister, LoP, Speaker, Dy Chairman RS. Only Lokpal includes an 'Eminent Jurist' as a mandatory member of the Selection Committee (Section 4, Lokpal Act, 2013). Worked Solution: The Lokpal Act, 2013 mandates a 5-member selection committee including an eminent jurist nominated by the President. Other bodies lack the 'eminent jurist' criterion in their appointment panels.

questions.text: The table below shows the approximate lengths of four major Indian river systems. Using the unit-digit method for addition, what is the unit digit of the sum of their lengths (in km)? | River System | Approx. Length (km) | | :--- | :--- | | Ganga | 2,525 | | Godavari | 1,465 | | Krishna | 1,400 | | Narmada | 1,312 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Add only unit digits: 5 (Ganga) + 5 (Godavari) + 0 (Krishna) + 2 (Narmada) = 12. Unit digit of sum is 2. No need to add thousands. Worked Solution: 2525 + 1465 + 1400 + 1312. Unit digits: 5+5+0+2 = 12. Unit digit is 2. Full sum = 6702 (verification).

questions.text: As per the table below showing Census 2011 data for four states, what is the approximate total number of literates in State B and State D combined (in Crores)? | State | Population (Cr) | Literacy Rate (%) | |-------|-----------------|-------------------| | A | 10 | 70 | | B | 8 | 80 | | C | 12 | 65 | | D | 6 | 85 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Approximate multiplication. State B: 8 × 0.80 = 6.4 Cr. State D: 6 × 0.85 = 5.1 Cr. Sum ≈ 11.5 Cr. Option elimination confirms 11.5 is the only plausible sum. Full: Literates B = 8 × 80/100 = 6.4 Cr. Literates D = 6 × 85/100 = 5.1 Cr. Total = 11.5 Cr.

questions.text: Arrange the following Sufi Silsilahs (Orders) in the chronological order of their establishment/arrival in India: 1. Chishti Order 2. Suhrawardi Order 3. Naqshbandi Order 4. Qadiri Order Select the correct code:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Memorize arrival sequence: Chishti (Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, ~1192 AD) -> Suhrawardi (Bahauddin Zakariya, ~13th Cent) -> Qadiri (15th Cent, Makhdum Jahaniyan) -> Naqshbandi (Khwaja Baqi Billah, ~1582 AD, Late Mughal). Step-by-step: 1. Chishti Order: Established by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in Ajmer late 12th century (Earliest). 2. Suhrawardi Order: Established by Sheikh Bahauddin Zakariya in Multan early 13th century (Second). 3. Qadiri Order: Introduced in India in 15th century by Sayyid Muhammad Ghawth / Makhdum Jahaniyan (Third). 4. Naqshbandi Order: Introduced by Khwaja Baqi Billah in late 16th century (Latest). Sequence: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the approximate sectoral distribution of India's Gross Value Added (GVA) at current prices for a recent fiscal year, which sector's share is closest to the combined share of the other two sectors? | Sector | Share (%) | | :--- | :--- | | Agriculture & Allied | 18.3 | | Industry | 26.2 | | Services | 55.5 |

options.label: D
options.text: None; no sector exceeds the sum of the other two

questions.solution: Shortcut: Check if any single value > 50%. Since total is 100%, a sector > 50% is automatically greater than the sum of the other two (which must be < 50%). Services at 55.5% > 50%, so it is the answer instantly. Worked Solution: Sum of Agriculture (18.3) + Industry (26.2) = 44.5%. Services share is 55.5%. Since 55.5 > 44.5, Services share is greater than the combined share of Agriculture and Industry.

questions.text: With reference to the three new Criminal Laws enacted in 2023 (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam), which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: They came into force on 26th January 2024.

options.label: B
options.text: The offence of 'Sedition' under Section 124A of the IPC has been retained verbatim in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

options.label: C
options.text: Community Service has been introduced as a form of punishment for the first time in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

options.label: D
options.text: The new laws are not applicable to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options using key factual anchors. Option A is wrong because the notified date of commencement is July 1, 2024, not Republic Day. Option B is wrong because 'Sedition' (Sec 124A IPC) has been repealed and replaced by a new offence 'Acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India' (Sec 150 BNS). Option D is wrong because post-Article 370 abrogation, Central laws apply directly to J&K. Option C remains as the only plausible major reform highlight. Worked Solution: The three Bills were passed in Dec 2023, received Presidential Assent on Dec 25, 2023, and were notified to come into force on July 1, 2024. The BNS introduces 'Community Service' (Section 4(f)) as a new punishment for petty offences (e.g., attempt to commit suicide, public servant unlawfully engaging in trade, non-appearance in response to proclamation). Sedition is replaced, not retained. The laws extend to the whole of India including J&K.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Priority Sector Lending (PSL) Targets and Actual Achievement (as % of Adjusted Net Bank Credit) for a recent fiscal year, which sector recorded the largest shortfall (deficit) in percentage points relative to its target? | Sector | Target (%) | Achievement (%) | | :--- | :---: | :---: | | Agriculture | 18.0 | 17.0 | | Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) | 7.5 | 8.0 | | Export Credit | 2.0 | 0.5 | | Social Infrastructure | 5.0 | 4.5 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Mentally compute (Target - Achievement) for each; ignore sectors where Achievement > Target (surplus). Agriculture: 1.0 pp; MSME: -0.5 pp (surplus); Export Credit: 1.5 pp; Social Infra: 0.5 pp. Export Credit has the highest deficit. Worked: Shortfall = Target % - Achievement %. Agriculture = 18.0 - 17.0 = 1.0 pp. MSME = 7.5 - 8.0 = -0.5 pp (surplus, eliminate). Export Credit = 2.0 - 0.5 = 1.5 pp. Social Infrastructure = 5.0 - 4.5 = 0.5 pp. Maximum shortfall is 1.5 pp for Export Credit.

questions.text: Under Article 368 of the Constitution of India, which one of the following categories of Constitutional Amendment Bills requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States before being presented to the President for assent?

options.label: A
options.text: A Bill seeking to alter the boundaries of an existing State

options.label: B
options.text: A Bill seeking to amend the provisions relating to the election of the President of India

options.label: C
options.text: A Bill seeking to amend the Directive Principles of State Policy

options.label: D
options.text: A Bill seeking to abolish the Legislative Council of a State

questions.solution: Shortcut: Only amendments affecting the 'Federal Structure' (List in Art 368 proviso: Art 54, 55, 73, 162, 241, Ch IV Part V, Ch V Part VI, Ch I Part XI, Seventh Schedule, Representation of States in Parliament, Art 368 itself) require State ratification. Step-by-step: 1. Option A (Art 3/4): Requires Simple Majority of Parliament only. 2. Option B (Art 54/55 - Election of President): Explicitly listed in Art 368 proviso. Requires Special Majority of Parliament + Ratification by 1/2 States. 3. Option C (DPSP): Requires Special Majority of Parliament only (Art 368 general). 4. Option D (Art 169): Requires Special Majority of Parliament + Resolution by concerned State Legislative Assembly (not ratification by 1/2 States).
